one_line: Nvidia and Dropbox push AI infrastructure, while Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash and Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoints arrive.

themes.title: Nvidia and Dropbox expand AI infrastructure
themes.text: Nvidia says its full-stack codesign of GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software raises useful work per byte of memory, with HBM capacity per GPU up about 3% and agentic throughput per dollar up to 30x on SemiAnalysis AgentX. Its Vera CPU is reported to run AI agents 1.5-2.2x faster than leading x86 CPUs with up to 1.6x more agents per watt, while Dropbox announced it will buy Tigris Data for $350 million to support its DBX Agent Cloud platform for AI model and agent developers.

stories.headline: Nvidia uses full‑stack codesign to boost AI memory efficiency
Nvidia vera cpu offers higher agent throughput and better power efficiency

themes.title: New video and simulation models released
themes.text: Google DeepMind released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a generative video model that creates native 15-second clips with multi-turn conversational editing at $0.07 per second for 720p, a 30% cost reduction from the prior version. Nvidia also released four open-weight Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoints built on a 16-billion-parameter model, each generating interactive world simulations and multi-sensor driving scenes.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model with 15-second clips
Nvidia adds four open-weight Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoints for interactive simulation

themes.title: Enterprise and interface agent tooling
themes.text: Mistral AI said its Studio platform now supports the Le Chonk multimodal model, letting enterprises build and deploy agents, workflows and apps on cloud, VPC or on-premises while retaining control over data and infrastructure. Separately, researchers proposed meta access, a structured, permissioned view of a software interface that lets LLM chat agents read and modify UI state, demonstrated in a prototype called Meta Chat.

stories.headline: Mistral launches Studio Le Chonk platform for enterprise AI deployment
Researchers propose meta‑access framework to extend LLM chat interfaces

themes.title: AI fraud, protests and safety probes
themes.text: Three people were indicted in New York for allegedly using AI to impersonate corporate executives and attorneys in a $129 million fraud scheme over more than a year and a half. More than 100 activists broke into the construction site of a Microsoft AI data centre in Amsterdam, the start of two days of protests in 15-16 European countries calling for a pause on large-scale data centre construction. Researchers also introduced VLA-Tug, a lightweight latent probe that raises early failure detection in vision-language-action models by up to 30%.
